finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the `u` query parameter is passed straight to URI.open, which fetches any http/https/ftp URL server-side. It also follows redirects. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is a non-blind SSRF. It can reach cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), localhost services and internal hosts.

trace.note: params[:u] passed directly to URI.open (open-uri) and read
first 400 bytes of the response returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist, no private-range or metadata blocking, no auth. open-uri follows redirects, so redirect-based bypass is moot. /trusted (app.rb:12-16) is SAFE: its host allowlist is enforced via halt and checked against the same uri.host that Net::HTTP.get connects to, and Net::HTTP.get does not follow redirects. /version (app.rb:18-20) is SAFE: constant URL.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the request parameter params[:u] straight to URI.open(...).read with no auth, allowlist, or scheme/host check, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes to the caller.
